column1: # Forge convention tag paths and the c: tag each one became, for NeoForge and for Forge 26.1+.
#   FORGE_PATH      the path of a forge: tag, such as ingots/iron for forge:ingots/iron
#   C_PATH          the path of the c: tag that replaced it, or = when the path is unchanged
#   NEOFORGE_SINCE  the first Minecraft version whose newest NeoForge build ships that c: tag,
#                   with every later newest build through 26.3 shipping it too
#   NEOFORGE_ALSO   optional, comma-separated earlier Minecraft versions whose newest NeoForge
#                   build ships that c: tag although a later version's newest build drops it
#                   again (NeoForge 21.1.262 ships c:tools/wrench, 21.2.1-beta and 21.3.100 do not)
# NeoForge dropped Forge's forge: tags for c: ones in 1.20.5. Forge kept both families through
# 1.21.11 and dropped all but a few forge: tags in 26.1. Every c: tag here is shipped by Forge
# 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3 (the newest build of each), so a row applies to every
#   - every forge: tag the Forge 1.20.1 jar ships whose meaning survived, matched by path or
#     by NeoForge's own legacy-name list, then checked by comparing resolved members (Forge
#     1.20.1 with vanilla 1.20.1 against NeoForge 21.11 with vanilla 1.21.11)
#   - community forge: names NeoForge's legacy-name list maps to a c: tag, kept only where the
#     two names are spellings of the same thing (cookie and cookies to foods/cookie)
# A forge: tag whose c: counterpart means something else is left out, so its references keep
# their forge: name: stained glass colors that collapsed into c:glass_blocks, raw ore blocks
# that NeoForge points at the refined storage blocks, and tags with no lasting c: tag at all.
